02-context-and-examples.html 7/10. A newcomer would struggle most with the ten-message test in Step 4: it packs a four-part procedure, the label 'Other' and the idea of a fair test into one dense paragraph.

02-context-and-examples.html 7/10. A newcomer would grasp why background and examples help, but would struggle most with the Step 4 test: its procedure is one dense paragraph and it never says which examples to reuse.
02-context-and-examples.html 7/10.

02-context-and-examples.html 7/10. A newcomer would grasp the idea of examples and marked pasted text, but would stall in Step 4, where it is unclear which ten messages to test and whether both runs must keep the same label list.

02-context-and-examples.html 7/10. A newcomer would mostly struggle with the Step 4 test: its instructions are muddled, it never says to keep the example messages out of the test, and its made-up results read like real ones.

02-context-and-examples.html 7/10. A newcomer would struggle most in Step 4: the lesson never says to decide the right labels before running the test, or to run each version in a fresh chat, so the score has no clear meaning.

01-what-a-prompt-is.html 8/10, 02-context-and-examples.html 7/10. A newcomer would struggle most with the second lesson's test step, because it says to compare labels with and without examples but never shows how to run ten messages through an assistant and score them.
